note: Costed remediation options. The agent may rank and explain these entries; it may not invent new ones. `expected_gain` is AP50 points recorded per option and is what the simulated runner replays.

options.rationale: Suppress out-of-scope classes that dominate low-elevation false positives; the bottleneck is precision, not capacity, so retraining is wasted spend.
Drop detections that do not persist for k frames; removes single-frame clutter without touching the detector.
High-elevation frames push objects to ~10 px; tiled inference restores effective resolution at a fraction of retraining cost.
The mid-elevation peak followed by a tail drop indicates an under-represented oblique regime; targeted perspective augmentation attacks the coverage gap directly.
Inverse-frequency sampling over pitch bins equalises the per-bin effective sample count.
Test-time augmentation recovers part of the tail drop at low cost; useful as a stopgap while a retrain is scheduled.
When the top-1 class changes with viewpoint, the shared classification head is trading classes off against each other; class-balanced weighting decouples them.
A per-viewpoint-group auxiliary head lets the shared trunk keep one representation while classes specialise.
No single detector wins at every viewpoint; routing by an estimated viewpoint bin turns instability into a per-bin best-of.
A frozen-backbone pitch classifier is 91.7% accurate at bin level, which is enough to route to the best detector per bin.
